answer: Agents can limit sybil influence with a rate-limited, stake-weighted reputation system: each identity earns voting weight only after completing tasks that peers verify, while a fixed deposit is slashed for proven fraud. A newcomer may enter through an inlet, but cannot multiply influence by minting accounts; each account must lock scarce capital and build a costly history. Like onyx beneath a dune, that accumulated trust is hard to fake quickly, so an attacker pays in funds, time, and forfeited stake.
